**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/10 (Mon) 22:51
- [USER] User inquired about measures Lesotho is taking to improve access to education for its citizens.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lesotho introduced a policy of free primary education in 2000, which has helped to increase enrolment and retention rates.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Government has allocated funds to construct new schools and classrooms in rural areas and refurbish existing ones, emphasizing the development of classrooms, libraries, laboratories, and other facilities necessary for quality education.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Government of Lesotho has launched initiatives to improve teacher quality, including train-the-trainer programs, mentoring programs, and professional development opportunities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Government is reviewing and developing the curriculum in line with international standards, emphasizing competency-based learning to prepare students for the world of work.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lesotho has formed partnerships with international organizations and private companies to provide access to technology and e-learning resources, introducing new teaching methods and improving access to educational materials in remote areas.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Various scholarship and bursary programs have been implemented to assist vulnerable and disadvantaged groups in gaining access to education, with the government providing scholarships for deserving students to study in local and international universities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lesotho provides adult education programs to help citizens who missed out on formal education acquire basic literacy and numeracy skills, including classroom-based instruction and distance learning programs.
- [USER] User asked for more information about the impact of free primary education in Lesotho and its effect on literacy rates.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The net enrolment rate for primary school in Lesotho increased from 69% in 1999 to 87% in 2019, indicating improved access to education.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The impact of free primary education on literacy rates is complicated; while access has increased, challenges related to quality education persist, including insufficient infrastructure, low teacher morale, and limited teaching materials.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The adult literacy rate in Lesotho was approximately 79% in 2018, and the literacy rate for youth aged 15-24 years was estimated to be around 89%.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite challenges, free primary education is viewed as a positive step towards improving access to education, but further investment is needed to enhance quality.
- [USER] User expressed concern about the challenges Lesotho faces in achieving better literacy rates and asked about other challenges.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Poverty significantly affects access to education, particularly in rural areas, where families may lack resources to send children to school.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Limited
